summary: The audit checks the core courses (COMM 300, 301, 302A, 302B and 302C), two advanced methods courses, and three graduate COMM courses, each required course with a B or better (an S for COMM 300 and 301), and 135 units in all. A course counts as either a methods or a substantive course, not both. You check by hand the three PhD-level substantive seminars from three different faculty, that the courses are taught by Communication PhD faculty, methods courses your advisor approves beyond the list, and the area exam, teaching, research projects, candidacy, oral exam and dissertation.

PIYD5qrC.why: "Two advanced research methods courses approved by the academic advisor and the DGS. The following courses are preapproved: COMM 314 and COMM 318." The data's list leaves both out, so they are added. Notes: "Courses must be completed by the end of Spring quarter of year 2 with grades of 'B' or above." Courses the advisor and DGS approve beyond the list are moved in by hand. Grading: "Students must earn a B or higher in all required courses for the PhD, except for COMM 300 and COMM 301, which require an S."

tsncPqkz.why: "Three substantive COMM courses designed for PhD students (e.g., 300-level seminars) from three different Communication PhD faculty and another three different graduate level COMM courses from COMM PhD faculty". The PhD-level courses are given only by example, so they are moved in by hand; the other three are graduate-level (200 and above) COMM courses. Who teaches each course is checked by hand. Grading: "Students must earn a B or higher in all required courses for the PhD, except for COMM 300 and COMM 301, which require an S."
